subject: history
title: Threats and Triumphs Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the threats Elizabeth faced — and how she defeated the Spanish Armada in 1588.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Mary Queen of Scots, Catholic plots and the Spanish Armada.
final_note: You learned how Mary QoS, Catholic plots and Spain threatened Elizabeth — and how she beat them.

Burning vessels sent into the Armada at Calais

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mary Queen of Scots fled to England in 1568.

As a Catholic with a claim to the throne, she was a magnet for plots. Elizabeth kept her prisoner for 19 years. The Ridolfi, Throckmorton and Babington Plots all tried to put Mary on the throne.

Walsingham, Elizabeth's spymaster, intercepted Mary's coded letters in the 1586 Babington Plot.

Mary was tried and beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle in February 1587. King Philip II of Spain — a devout Catholic — now had his excuse to invade England.

In July 1588 Philip sent around 130 ships and 30,000 men.

English fire ships scattered the Armada at Calais. The Battle of Gravelines and fierce storms wrecked the fleet — only about half the ships made it home. Elizabeth gave her Tilbury speech.

mcqs.q: In what year was Mary Queen of Scots executed?
Roughly how many ships did Philip II send in the Spanish Armada?
What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
